notes:
Primary contact: CTO (Jonas Faraday) + Head of Search Eng (Priya Malhotra).
Use-case summary: internal developer code search + embedded RAG for engineering docs. Large code corpus (50M+ files / blobs including monorepos), frequent commits -> need incremental re-indexing (every 2–6 hours). Reranking must be applied post-retrieval to improve precision on code snippets (we heard 'current recall OK but top-3 relevance noisy').
Latency targets: P95 end-to-end rerank+return <200ms for dev IDE queries; batch analytics queries can be slower. Throughput: spikes during CI windows (burst to 10k qps for short windows).
Cost constraints: internal budget target $0.01–$0.03 per query average across mixed traffic; interested in Optimize recommendations (batching, cache, quant profiles).
Model preferences: open checkpoints acceptable (Llama2, Orca/Mistral variants); want ability to run quantized LLMs on-prem. Must support KV-cache for code context and streaming optional.
Security & compliance: SSO/SAML + SCIM required, audit logging with 1-year retention, KMS integration mandatory. Data residency: primary US, but EU dev teams require EU-region replica. Air-gapped option for a small subset of repos (regulated clients).
POC ask: Redwood to demonstrate indexing 10M code files, show incremental re-index throughput, reranking lift on standard dev prompts, end-to-end latency measurements, and per-query cost estimates.
Quote from call: 'If you can keep top-1 accuracy up and latency under 200ms we can justify paying for the dedicated path.'
Decision criteria: 1) measurable rerank quality lift vs baseline, 2) predictable unit economics and clear autoscaling, 3) SSO/SAML + audit controls validated, 4) acceptable on-prem footprint and offline install docs.
